decisions.statement: The refusals are written beside the agent's own page.
The file is named for the property the agent page type declares for that kind of refusal.
A landing's refusals and an audit's refusals are kept under two properties.
A run keeping one of them leaves the other as it was.
A path under no TypeScript name keeps no refusals.
A run replaces the file rather than appending to the file.
A run refusing nothing takes the file away.
One blank line parts two refusals in the file.
A refusal set one answer holds is handed back whole.
A refusal set past that ceiling is handed back as a pointer to the file.
The pointer names the path and the call opening that path.
The pointer says every refusal is there rather than that each one is whole.
An audit's refusals reach here from a row holding each text to a ceiling.
One wording names that path and that call, wherever a pointer is said.
A caller keeping refusals is handed back the path those refusals went to.
A run that wrote no file hands back no path.
How many bytes one answer has is read from the module stating that count.
A file the machine could not write leaves the refusals handed back whole.
Nothing here judges what a refusal says.

definition: the refusals an agent's last landing or last audit answered with
